# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura KS-754 / PR #914 @ `311dc1ae4` — TIER 1 round 1, 2026-09-09 11:09 → 11:25) | **GO WITH FINDINGS on the PR the entire repo was blocked behind — and it DROVE the question rather than reasoning about it, on a live Postgres it stood up and removed.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Q1 was the blocker-shaped question and it answered it with three driven cells and two independent controls:** a throw at step 12 skips the USER_ERASED fan-out **after** the crypto-shred. `S3` head+injection → `success=false DEK=1 USER_ERASED=0`; **`CTL-A` head, injection OFF** isolates the injection as cause; **`CTL-B` base + the SAME injection** holds DB and injection fixed and varies **only the code**, isolating the rethrow as cause of the lost fan-out. **Both controls can fail independently of the thing tested** — the independence rule, satisfied by construction rather than asserted. **Then it drove RECOVERABILITY rather than assuming it:** a second attempt with the injection lifted fully repairs the DSR, while the base-code control never repairs — *"both attempts succeed and the DSR stays processing with no actor forever."* **So it converted Wednesday's worry into a bounded, self-correcting, NET-IMPROVEMENT verdict, with the residual named:** between the failed attempt and the retry, originate's copy is destroyed while four subscribers still hold theirs. **The fan-out scope was MEASURED, not estimated — exactly four subscribers, each named with its file and line.** **F-2 found a real regression by driving three ids over real HTTP against the mounted router on both SHAs**, and the third row is the one that matters: on develop a legitimate admin PATCH is told *"DSR not found"* about a DSR that exists, and #914 fixes it — so the finding is *"it also converts a client error into a server error"*, not *"it broke something"*. **Bounded honestly: admin-only, no data impact (row read back from pg after every case), no info disclosure under `NODE_ENV=production`.** ⚠ **AND IT CAUGHT ITS OWN INSTRUMENT FIRST, which is why the rest is trustworthy: the Secuura tree sits on a different branch, so reading product files in place measured the WRONG CODE — its first instrument returned two identical results for cells that had to differ.** Both trees then reconstructed by SHA into its own scratchpad and hash-matched against repo objects. Its own line, adopted: **"if a future gate drives this repo's source, reconstruct by SHA first; do not read in place."** **Hygiene: tree clean and branch unchanged at close, its own `qa914-pg` container removed and verified gone, `:6882` never used as evidence and both shared containers confirmed to predate the pass. AND IT MAILED ITS VERDICT AND WROTE A REPORT FILE** — the launcher's new mail guard working on its first outing, after the #912 verdict had to be recovered from a session transcript. |
| Secuura/Blockchain s156 (`%10`, 2026-09-09 10:33 → 10:50 AEST — booted, plan-confirmed, built and landed in SEVENTEEN MINUTES) | **THE BUMP KAM RULED: five advisories removed, zero manifests changed, PR #915 on origin — and it corrected Wednesday's brief TWICE before building, then caught THREE false instruments of its own during the work.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Verified independently by Wednesday, not taken from the wrap:** `fe0fd640c709084e25569d5f61bc584a02d499e5` at `refs/heads/feature/ks-1024-bump-nodemailer-morgan` via `ls-remote`, with a positive control (develop present) and a negative control (a bogus ref returns 0 lines). **PRE-BUILD, it corrected the brief twice, both in our favour:** morgan is `^1.10.0` not the

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.

> ## ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 ~08:1x — Kam SENT the re-issue same hour ("email sent").
> Landed i
